sources.note: Main site. Describes athenaOne as 'Integrated, AI-Native Healthcare Software & Services.' Navigation reveals full product taxonomy, specialty support, and customer segments.
athenaOne product page. Confirms three-module structure: athenaClinicals (EHR), athenaCollector (billing/RCM), athenaCommunicator (patient engagement).
ONC certification page. Lists four certified modules: athenaClinicals, athenaClinicals for HHS, athenaPractice, athenaFlow. Contains AI/PDSI governance disclosures and Real World Testing plan links.

Terms and conditions page. Contains product descriptions, metrics (315M+ claims/year, 8% lower no-show rate), patent listings for athenaCollector/athenaClinicals/Epocrates, and implementation cost information.
Enterprise page. Describes Enterprise EHR, Enterprise RCM Services, Patient Engagement, and Staffing Services. Includes hospital customer quote from Doctors' Memorial Hospital.
Blog post explaining the three-module naming structure of athenaOne.
athenaCommunicator page. Describes patient portal, secure messaging, self-scheduling, digital intake, bill pay, automated outreach campaigns.
athenaTelehealth page. HIPAA-compliant video visits, up to 4 participants, live captions, 3,000+ active customers.
athenaCollector/practice management page. Scheduling, eligibility, claims (30,000+ rules), denials management, payment posting.
RCM services page. Covers both athenaCollector and athenaIDX. Percentage-of-collections business model.
Marketplace page. 500+ third-party apps across 50 digital health capabilities and 60 specialties.
Developer portal. 800+ API endpoints, FHIR R4, SMART on FHIR, HL7 interfaces.
Interoperability page. CommonWell (90% of customers, 84,000+ care sites), Carequality, TEFCA participation.
Specialty practices page. Lists 25+ supported specialties with specialty-specific workflow configurations.
Fall 2025 release notes. 185 features/enhancements including AI-powered clinical summaries, Chart Assist, AI document labeling.
Patient portal FAQ. Describes portal capabilities: view records, secure messaging, self-scheduling, bill pay, digital intake.
Wikipedia article. Comprehensive corporate history: founded 1997, IPO 2007, Veritas acquisition 2018 ($5.7B), Virence merger 2019, Bain/H&F acquisition 2022 ($17B).
TechTarget definition. Confirms cloud-based SaaS model, three-module structure, and Virence Health merger history.
G2 reviews. 3.5/5 stars (~102 reviews). Users praise auto-filling and navigation; complaints about pricing, customer service, weak mobile/telehealth capabilities.
KLAS vendor ratings. Software score 81.2, services score 80.7. Positioned alongside Epic as 'clear market leaders' in ambulatory care.
2026 Best in KLAS press release. Five awards including first-time recognition for 75+ physician Ambulatory EHR. 47 lifetime awards.
Capterra reviews. 3.8/5 across 835+ reviews. Detailed user feedback on charting, scheduling, billing, and support. Top complaints: customer support, implementation, system performance.
Software Advice reviews. Shares review pool with Capterra. Users describe charting as faster than Epic, praise customizable workflows, but cite billing collection gaps.
Definitive Healthcare ambulatory EHR rankings (Oct 2025). athenahealth: 5,801 installations, 6.9% market share (3rd behind Epic at 19.5% and eClinicalWorks at 11.9%).
Enlyft market data. ~6,900 customers, 64% small orgs, 95% US-based. 40% Hospital & Health Care, 24% Medical Practice.
6sense market share data. 16.74% EHR market share (different methodology from Definitive HC), 6,757 customer companies.
EHR Guide review. 8.3/10 overall. Confirms product components and cloud-based architecture.
MD Clarity review. Confirms athenaOne module structure and RCM capabilities.
Business.com review (2026). Covers features, pricing model, and user experience across all modules.
July 2020 press release. Centricity Business rebranded to athenaIDX. Confirms IDX Systems → GE → Virence → athenahealth lineage.
Healthcare IT News coverage of athenaIDX rebrand. Confirms it's a separate enterprise RCM product distinct from athenaCollector.
February 2022 acquisition announcement. Bain Capital and Hellman & Friedman acquire athenahealth for $17B.
HCI Innovation Group analysis of athenahealth's hospital IT strategy. Details RazorInsights and webOMR acquisitions, University of Toledo co-development partnership.
Healthcare IT News on webOMR acquisition from Beth Israel Deaconess. Inpatient EHR developed over 30 years, intended for 100+ bed hospitals.
Healthcare IT News on University of Toledo Medical Center co-development partnership (2016). Building inpatient EHR as 'disruptive alternative to legacy health IT.'
FHIR API documentation. Confirms FHIR R4 support, SMART on FHIR, US Core Implementation Guide compliance.

EHI export FHIR resource listing. Lists all supported FHIR resources including custom billing resources (Adjustment, BillingStatement, Charge, Claim, Collection, Deductible, Eligibility, PatientInsurance, Payment).
HIT Consultant coverage of AI features in athenaClinicals: ambient-sourced diagnosis, clinically inferred diagnoses, Chart Assist GenAI.
KLAS ambulatory EHR suites report coverage. Notes athenahealth and Epic as 'clear market leaders' with practices 'ditching point solutions' in favor of integrated suites.
